newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 2.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's edition of Daily Variety:
NEW YORK - For a second year in a row, ABC, a unit of Walt Disney Co, has scored a Christmas week primetime Nielsens victory despite the lowest regular-season weeklong average in its history.
HOLLYWOOD - The domestic box office year concluded on a high note of close to $5.76 billion according to initial holiday reporting. The figure represents an increase of 7.9 percent from 1995.

NEW YORK - With the new content-ratings system officially taking effect on Wednesday, the networks are allotting valuable promo time to make sure viewers understand the new labels slapped on their shows.

NEW YORK - Entertainment investors are hoping for a happy new year on Wall Street after one of the worst years in memory, but chances for an upturn in entertainment stocks are dependent on debt-reducing moves at companies like Time Warner Inc and Viacom Inc.

HOLLYWOOD - Those velociraptors in the sequel to Jurassic Park aren't the only once-extinct creatures roaming studio lots these days. Studio screenwriters, a fixture during Hollywood's Golden Age, also seem to be making a comeback. A growing number of studios and production companies are inking deals with seasoned scribes in order to lock in their services for original scripts and rewrites.
HOLLYWOOD - Developers are in a rush to snatch up land and make their fortunes building studio soundstages. The latest project: 16 soundstages, built on an auto wrecking yard in Sun Valley.
